---
title: "C · Read performance — results"
---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Bottom line.** For **subsets** (a site, a county), **virtual Zarr references** (VirtualiZarr →
icechunk) win everywhere: they fetch only the needed chunks, concurrently — 0.4–0.6 s in-region and
1–4 s through slow HTTPS/NCCS-like links for a 33 × 33 window, moving < 1 MB, where file-oriented readers
move 30–2,000 MB. For **whole granules**, a single streamed download beats everything. Library
**defaults are the main hazard**: h5py on `s3fs` (50 MiB blocks) pulls ~0.5–0.9 GB for a 33 × 33 window,
xarray + h5netcdf on `s3fs` 1.3–2.1 GB, GDAL's 16 KB requests ~900–2,200 requests; one fsspec setting
(`blockcache`, 8 MiB, as `earthaccess` uses) or a few GDAL options fix most of it. Two robustness
gaps decide what works on noisy links: **icechunk 2.3 does not retry transient 5xx/SlowDown on virtual
chunks** (full-granule reads with thousands of requests fail), and **HDF5's ROS3 driver cannot follow
Earthdata's per-request 303 redirect**. MODIS HDF4 can only be downloaded — unless VirtualiZarr/kerchunk
are patched ([details](https://github.com/ashiklom/simon-code-research/blob/main/l2-swath-geolocation/patches/README.md)), after which it virtualises like HDF5.
:::

## Small window (one site)

![](figures/read_window_site.png)

Median seconds for a 33 × 33 window of latitude, longitude and LST (geolocation + L2 file):

| Reader | VIIRS in-region | VIIRS Earthdata HTTPS | ECOSTRESS in-region | ECOSTRESS NCCS | MB moved (ECOSTRESS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| icechunk virtual refs | **0.54** | **2.8** | **0.36** | **2.9** | **0.8** |
| h5py ROS3 | 1.8 | fails (redirect) | 2.1 | 9.0 | 34 |
| h5py + fsspec blockcache 8 MiB | 2.3 | 8.7 | 3.0 | 14 | 115 |
| h5py + fsspec defaults | 9.7 | 15 | 18 | 18 | 916 |
| GDAL tuned / defaults | 6.3 / 41 | 13 / 113 | 22 / 118 | 66 / timeout | 423 / 791 |
| xarray + h5netcdf (fsspec) | 26 | 49 | 42 | 40 | 2,093 |
| download whole file | 2.1 | 5.5 | 16 | 110 | 983 |

The ranking is almost entirely *requests × latency + bytes ÷ bandwidth*: the virtual references know
the exact byte range of every chunk (no metadata crawling) and fetch the 25–45 chunks in parallel.
File-oriented readers first walk the HDF5 metadata with many small reads and then over-fetch through
their caches. ROS3 is efficient (it caches the first 16 MiB, which holds the metadata of these files)
but HDF5 1.14 fails on the HTTPS redirect ("could not find Content-Length"). On the NCCS-like profile
(heavy-tailed latency, stalls, 0.5 % 5xx), sequential readers suffer most; retries matter more than
speed (xarray via fsspec failed 2 of 3 repetitions with a 503).

## Full granule

![](figures/read_full.png)

For whole granules the picture flips: **download-then-read** (one GET) costs 3 s (VIIRS) and
21 s (ECOSTRESS, 983 MB) in-region and stays within 2–3× of that on every profile, while chunk-wise
readers pay per request — icechunk needs ~3,000 requests for VIIRS lat/lon/LST (9 s in-region) and fails
over HTTPS/NCCS because a single unretried 5xx aborts the read; ROS3 takes 185 s for ECOSTRESS in-region
(4,000 requests). Tuned GDAL is a robust all-rounder (22–84 s for ECOSTRESS).

## Requests and bytes

The proxy counts every request. Requests × latency and bytes ÷ bandwidth explain almost all of
the differences between readers:

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
bench = FileAttachment("data/site/read_bench.csv").csv({typed: true})
viewof rbSensor = Inputs.radio(["modis", "viirs", "ecostress"], {value: "viirs", label: "sensor"})
viewof rbTask = Inputs.radio(["window_site", "window_poly", "full"], {value: "window_site", label: "task"})
rbRows = {
  const sub = bench.filter(d => d.sensor === rbSensor && d.task === rbTask);
  const out = [];
  for (const [key, g] of d3.group(sub, d => d.reader + "|" + d.profile)) {
    const [reader, profile] = key.split("|");
    const ok = g.filter(d => d.seconds != null && !isNaN(d.seconds));
    out.push({reader, profile, "median s": ok.length ? d3.median(ok, d => d.seconds).toFixed(2) : "fail",
              "min–max s": ok.length ? `${d3.min(ok, d => d.seconds).toFixed(2)}–${d3.max(ok, d => d.seconds).toFixed(2)}` : "",
              ok: `${ok.length}/${g.length}`, requests: d3.median(ok, d => d.net_requests) ?? "",
              MB: ok.length && ok[0].net_bytes != null ? (d3.median(ok, d => d.net_bytes) / 1e6).toFixed(1) : "",
              redirects: d3.median(ok, d => d.net_redirects) ?? "",
              error: ok.length < g.length ? String(g.find(d => d.error)?.error ?? "").slice(0, 90) : ""});
  }
  const order = ["local", "zero_http", "zero_s3", "s3_in_region", "s3_cross_region", "https_earthdata", "nccs_portal"];
  return out.sort((a, b) => order.indexOf(a.profile) - order.indexOf(b.profile) || a.reader.localeCompare(b.reader));
}
Inputs.table(rbRows, {rows: 25})
```

## Building the virtual references

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
vb = FileAttachment("data/site/virtual_build.csv").csv({typed: true})
vbRows = {
  const out = [];
  for (const [key, g] of d3.group(vb, d => d.file + "|" + d.parser + "|" + d.profile)) {
    const [file, parser, profile] = key.split("|");
    const ok = g.filter(d => d.seconds != null && !isNaN(d.seconds));
    out.push({file: file.split("/")[1].slice(0, 28), parser, profile,
              "median s": ok.length ? d3.median(ok, d => d.seconds).toFixed(2) : "fail",
              requests: ok.length ? d3.median(ok, d => d.net_requests) ?? "" : "", MB: ok.length && ok[0].net_bytes != null ? (d3.median(ok, d => d.net_bytes) / 1e6).toFixed(1) : "",
              error: ok.length < g.length ? String(g.find(d => d.error)?.error ?? "").slice(0, 80) : ""});
  }
  return out;
}
Inputs.table(vbRows, {rows: 25})
```

Virtual references are an index: built once, reused for every read. Scanning the HDF5 file remotely
(VirtualiZarr `HDFParser` with its default 1 MiB block reader) touches **264 MB** of the 780 MB ECOSTRESS
GEO file (16 s in-region, 2 min over HTTPS) because these files are not "cloud-optimised" (chunk
indexes are scattered through the file). The **DMR++ sidecar** that NASA publishes for LP DAAC products
gives the same chunk map in **0.6 s / 1.6 MB**. For VNP21 the DMR++ path fails (string `_FillValue`,
same bug as the HDF5 path; fixed by the patch). LAADS publishes no DMR++ for MOD03/MYD03/VNP03MOD.
The patched HDF4 scan of MYD03 (37 MB) moves the whole file over S3 (2 requests) but 205 MB over HTTPS,
because fsspec's 5 MiB block cache thrashes as kerchunk seeks through HDF4 tags.

*Time budget.* To keep the run under ~6 h, each (reader, profile, task) stops repeating after 90 s,
whole-granule ECOSTRESS reads used only the six most informative readers, and default GDAL (which
already timed out at 300 s for the ECOSTRESS site window on the slow profiles) was not re-run for the
ECOSTRESS county window on those profiles.
